# Logistics

This homework consists of a portfolio visualization and an associated written report ("write-up").

You will create a single visualization with at least one interactive feature (this can be an external feature like a button, or an on-plot feature like clicking or brushing).

Your visualization must **visualize the results of a clustering algorithm, dimensionality-reduction algorithm, topic model, OR deep learning model.**

## Submission Instructions

As always, you do **not need to submit any data files**, such as .csv files.

Please submit:

- **Your code file(s), such as .Rmd or .R file(s)**

- **Your write-up**, as a separate, well-formatted PDF or Word or other text document.

- **Evidence of interactivity**, either through a series of screenshots, 

## Grading

#### Visualization [25 points]

**Design Choices [20 points]**: The visualization(s) should effectively and intuitively answer meaningful questions. Your design choices should go above and beyond defaults, and show critical thinking as well as attention to detail towards aiding the viewer in understanding the takeaway(s) of the visualization. Strive to make your graphs as polished as possible; especially with choices such as layout, labels, sizes, themes, and colors. Though it may build from course examples, the submission should demonstrate independent and creative thinking.

**Problem Formulation [5 points]**: The context of the visualization is appropriately communicated, and all data are reported within context, rather than assuming prior familiarity with specific variable names or data collection methods, for example. (*You can still use field-specific terminology if your intended audience would know what it means, but any such terms should be explained in your write-up.*) The problem or question the visualization investigates should not have an obvious answer, and the visualization could have an audience beyond the course. 

#### Write-up [25 points]

**Discussion Quality [20 points]**: The write-up is thorough with respect to each prompt but not overly wordy and avoids technical jargon. Writing demonstrates critical thinking about the author's own workflows, decisions, and what information needs to be communicated to the viewer.

**Discussion Formatting [5 points]**: The write-up uses correct and engaging grammar (e.g. varied sentence length), and uses paragraphs/headers/other formatting to appropriately organize the text.

# Portfolio Visualization

Choose a dataset you are interested in visualizing. You may choose any dataset, including those from your personal studies/outside knowledge, or pick one from these suggested collections:

[TidyTuesday](https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday#datasets), [Kaggle](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets), [Google Dataset Search](https://datasetsearch.research.google.com/), [AWS Data Registry](https://registry.opendata.aws/), [Wisconsin DNR](https://data-wi-dnr.opendata.arcgis.com/), [IPUMS Census Data](https://www.ipums.org/), [538](https://github.com/fivethirtyeight/data/)

You can also run `data()` in your R console to see all of the built-in datasets in the packages that you have loaded.

With your chosen dataset, create one visualization with at least one interactive feature (can be external like a button, or on-plot like clicking and hovering). This visualization must **visualize the results of a clustering algorithm, dimensionality-reduction algorithm, topic model, OR deep learning model.**

# Write-up

**Write-ups have a word maximum of 500 words.** 

Write-ups should be aimed at someone with **no knowledge or interest in coding** (e.g. do not mention specific functions), but who is interested in understanding your visualization and how you developed it.

Please address the following prompts in your write-up:

* Provide a short description of the dataset, including:
  *   Where you found it (Please include a link and the author's/organization's name)
  *   A high-level mention of any important transformations you made to the dataset before visualizing
  *   What a single row of the (potentially transformed) dataset represents in real terms
  *   Any relevant criteria for being included/excluded from this dataset (e.g. does it cover certain years, certain cities, etc?)
  *   A brief explanation of any variables relevant to understanding the visualization; including units and brief background information where necessary. You do not need to cite specific variable names.
  
* The bulk of your write-up should answer these prompts about the design process:
  *   What is/are the main question(s) your visualization investigates, and who are the intended audience?
  
  *   **Interpret** your visualization for the audience, using **non-technical, plain language**, in a way that answers the main question(s) you just listed.
  *   Justify how your interactive element helps the viewer answer the main question(s) you just listed.
